definition: Learning a dynamics model of the environment and using it for planning or imagined rollouts (Dyna-style), instead of learning purely from real experience.
details: Learning a dynamics model of the environment and using it for planning or imagined rollouts (Dyna-style), instead of learning purely from real experience. Dramatically more sample efficient when the model is good; MuZero showed the model can be learned implicitly, planning in latent space without reconstructing observations.

explainer.lead: An RL approach that learns a dynamics model of the environment and uses it for planning or imagined rollouts, rather than learning purely from real experience. It matters because it is dramatically more sample efficient when the model is good.

tiers.eli5: Rather than trying everything for real, you learn how the world reacts, then practise inside your head before acting.
tiers.practitioner: Dyna-style loops alternate real experience with planning against the learned model. A pitfall is that a bad model misleads planning; MuZero showed the model can be learned implicitly, planning in latent space without reconstructing observations.
tiers.paperLevel: Learn a dynamics model of the environment and use it for planning or imagined rollouts; the limit is model error, which degrades imagined experience.

explainer.example: A learned model generates imagined rollouts that supplement limited real interactions to speed up policy learning.
